Arator apud Bedam in Act.}}∷ Peter & Iohn. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}} Vvho vvhen they vvere come, praied for them, that they might receiue the holy Gho{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}} For he vvas not yet come vpon any of them, but they vvere only baptized in the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}} Then {{sup|‖}} did they impo{{ls}}e their handes vpon them, {{sup|‖}} and they receiued the holy Gho{{ls}}t.⊣ {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}} And vvhen Simon had {{ls}}een that by the impo{{ls}}ition of the hand of the Apo{{ls}}tles, the holy Gho{{ls}}t vvas giuen, he {{sup|‖}} offered them money, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}} {{ls}}aying, Giue me al{{ls}}o this povver, that on vvhom{{ls}}oeuer I impo{{ls}}e my handes, he may receiue the holy Gho{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}} But Peter {{ls}}aid to him, Thy money be vvith thee vnto perdition: becau{{ls}}e thou ha{{ls}}t thought that the gift of God is purcha{{ls}}ed vvith money. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}} Thou ha{{ls}}t no part, nor lot in this vvord. For thy hart is not right before God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''{{lang|grc|μετανόησον ἀπὸ}} See Apocal. 9, 21.''}}∷ {{sup|‖}} Doe penance therfore from this thy vvickedne{{ls}}{{ls}}e: and pray to God, {{sup|‖}} if perhaps this cogitation of thy hart may be remitted thee. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}} For I {{ls}}ee thou art in the gall of bitternes and the obligation of iniquitie. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}} And Simon an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid, {{sup|‖}} Pray you for me to our Lord, that nothing come vpon me of the{{ls}}e things vvhich you haue {{ls}}aid. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}} And they in deede hauing te{{ls}}tified and {{ls}}poken the vvord of our Lord, returned to Hieru{{ls}}alem, and euangelized to many countries of the Samaritans.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epi{{ls}}tle vpon Thur{{ls}}day in Ea{{ls}}ter vveeke.}}∷ And an Angel of our Lord {{ls}}pake to Philippe, {{ls}}aying: Ari{{ls}}e, and goe tovvard the South, to the vvay that goeth dovvne from Hieru{{ls}}alem into Gaza: {{sup|‖}} this is de{{ls}}ert. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}} And ri{{ls}}ing he vvent. And behold, a man of Æthiopia, an eunuch, of great authoritie vnder Candáce the Queene of the Æthiopians, vvho vvas ouer al her trea{{ls}}ures, vvas come to Hieru{{ls}}alem {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note that this Æthiopian came to Hieru{{ls}}alem to adore, that is, on Pilgrimage. vvhere by vve may learne that it is an acceptable acte of religion to go from home to places of greater deuotiõ & {{ls}}anctificatiõ.}}∷ to adore: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}} and he vvas returning and {{ls}}itting vpon his chariot, and reading E{{ls}}ay the prophet. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}} And the Spirit {{ls}}aid to Philippe, Goe neere, and ioyne thy {{ls}}elf to this {{ls}}ame chariot. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}} And Philippe running therevnto, heard him reading E{{ls}}ay the prophet, and he {{ls}}aid: Trovve{{ls}}t thou that thou vnder{{ls}}tande{{ls}}t the things vvhich thou reade{{ls}}t? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}} Vvho {{ls}}aid, And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Scriptures are {{ls}}o vvritten that they can not be vnder{{ls}}tood vvithout an interpreter, as ea{{ls}}y as our Prote{{ls}}tants make them. See S. Hierom ''Ep. ad Paulinũ de omnibus diuinæ hi{{ls}}toriæ libris'', {{ls}}et in the beginning of latin bibles.}}∷ hovv can I, vnle{{ls}}{{ls}}e {{ls}}ome man {{ls}}hevv me? & he de{{ls}}ired Philippe that he vvould come vp and {{ls}}it vvith him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}} And the place of the {{ls}}cripture vvhich he did reade, vvas this: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Es. 53, 7.''}}* ''As a {{ls}}heepe to {{ls}}laughter vvas he led: and as a lambe before his {{ls}}hearer, vvithout voice, {{ls}}o did he not open his mouth''. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}} ''In humilitie his iudgement vvas taken avvay.''<noinclude>{{continues|His}}</noinclude>
